# pdns_zone (Resource)

Manages a PowerDNS DNS zone, including its SOA and nameserver (NS) records.

**Dynamic updates:** unless the server runs with `dnsupdate-require-tsig=yes` (PowerDNS 5.0+), a zone without dnsupdate keys accepts unsigned updates from `allow-dnsupdate-from`. Set that option, or `lock_dnsupdate = true` on older servers.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pdns_zone" "example_com" {
  name = "example.com."

  dnssec = false

  nameservers = [
    {
      hostname = "ns1",
      address  = "10.10.10.1"
    },
    {
      hostname = "ns2",
      address  = "10.10.10.2"
    }
  ]

  soa = {
    rname = "hostmaster"

    refresh = 10800
    retry   = 3600
    expire  = 604800
    ttl     = 3600
  }

}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The Name of the zone to be created. Must end with a dot
- `nameservers` (Attributes List) The nameservers of the Zone (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nameservers))
- `soa` (Attributes) The Start Of Authority (SOA) record parameters for the zone. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--soa))

### Optional

- `dnssec` (Boolean) Whether or not this zone is DNSSEC signed
- `kind` (String) The zone kind. One of `Native`, `Master`, `Slave`, `Producer` or `Consumer`. Defaults to `Native`.
- `lock_dnsupdate` (Boolean) Refuse unsigned RFC2136 dynamic updates for this zone, for servers without `dnsupdate-require-tsig`. By default PowerDNS only requires a signature while the zone's `TSIG-ALLOW-DNSUPDATE` metadata lists a key; while it is empty (a new zone, or after the last dnsupdate key was removed), unsigned updates from addresses permitted by `allow-dnsupdate-from` are accepted. With `true`, the provider keeps the placeholder `pdns-provider-dnsupdate-locked.` in that list, so only updates signed by keys attached with `pdns_zone_tsig_key` (`dnsupdate = true`) are accepted, and none while no key is attached. New zones are then created as `Slave` (which does not apply updates), locked and only then switched to their `kind`, so they never accept unlocked updates. Setting it to `false` removes the placeholder.

On PowerDNS 5.0 and later, prefer the server setting `dnsupdate-require-tsig=yes`: it refuses every update that is not signed by a key listed for the zone, for all zones and from the moment they exist, so this lock is not needed. Use the lock on 4.9 (which does not have the setting) or where the server configuration cannot be changed. The setting applies to every zone of the server; for per-zone control, also on 5.0+, leave `dnsupdate-require-tsig` off and set `lock_dnsupdate = true` only on the zones that must refuse unsigned updates. The placeholder is not a real key: never create a TSIG key named `pdns-provider-dnsupdate-locked` outside the provider (with `pdnsutil` or the API), as it would be allowed to perform dynamic updates of every zone with `lock_dnsupdate = true`. Defaults to `false`.
- `masters` (List of String) The primaries the zone is transferred from, as IP addresses with an optional port (`192.0.2.1`, `2001:db8::1`, `192.0.2.1:5300` or `[2001:db8::1]:5300`). Only valid for `kind = "Slave"` or `"Consumer"`; such zones are created with their primaries directly, also with `lock_dnsupdate = true` (the temporary `Slave` of a locked create is only used for the other kinds and has no primaries). Changes are applied in place.

### Read-Only

- `serial` (String) The serial of the zone

<a id="nestedatt--nameservers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nameservers`

Required:

- `hostname` (String) The hostname of the nameservers. Will be suffixed with the zone name if not ending with an explicit '.'. Use the fully qualified name (e.g. "example.com.") for the zone apex; "@" and empty names are rejected.

Optional:

- `address` (String) The IP Address of the nameserver. The provider manages it as the A (IPv4) or AAAA (IPv6) glue record at the hostname, holding exactly this address, so it can only be set for nameservers inside the zone. If that record is changed, extended or removed outside of Terraform, the next plan shows the difference and the apply restores it.


<a id="nestedatt--soa"></a>
### Nested Schema for `soa`

Required:

- `rname` (String) The RName of the SOA record. Represents the administrator's email address. It will be suffixed with the zone name unless ending with an explicit '.'. "@" and empty names are rejected.

Optional:

- `create_record` (Boolean) If set to false the provider will not create the SOA record
- `expire` (Number) If a secondary server does not get a response from the primary server for this amount of time, it should stop responding to queries for the zone.
- `refresh` (Number) The length of time (in seconds) secondary servers should wait before asking primary servers for the SOA record to see if it has been updated.
- `retry` (Number) The length of time a server should wait for asking an unresponsive primary nameserver for an update again.
- `ttl` (Number) TTL of the zone data

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Zones are imported by their name (with the trailing dot).
#
# soa and nameservers are read from the zone's records:
# - soa from the SOA record. create_record is true, unless the zone has the
#   default SOA record PowerDNS creates for zones without one; then it is
#   false, rname is read from it and the other soa values are their defaults.
# - nameservers from the NS records: first the primary nameserver of the SOA
#   record, then the others sorted by name (the order PowerDNS returns them in
#   depends on the backend). Hostnames inside the zone are relative to it ("ns1"), others
#   fully qualified. A hostname inside the zone gets its address from the A
#   record at that name, or else the AAAA record.
#
# Write names inside the zone relative to it, list the nameservers in the same
# order and set the address of every nameserver that has one, so the first
# plan after the import shows no changes. Otherwise that plan updates the zone
# to the configured values.
terraform import pdns_zone.example_com example.com.
```
